# A deliberately long chapter title for testing wrapping, running heads, navigation, and narrow print profiles {#sec-layout-stress}

This chapter is a pagination stress specimen, not manuscript filler. Its long
headings and labeled boundary paragraphs make subtle layout regressions visible
in every profile while keeping the source readable enough to diagnose a
failure. The chapter opener itself is also a stable marker for recto-page tests.

## A section heading long enough to wrap at six-by-nine trim without escaping the live area or obscuring its number {#sec-long-heading}

Long headings must remain complete in the contents, bookmarks, and accessible
document structure. On the printed page they may wrap, but the number and text
must remain visibly associated, no word may cross the live-area boundary, and a
heading must stay with the content that follows it. A running head is secondary
navigation rather than the canonical title, so it may use a compact treatment
when the full heading cannot fit on one furniture line.

### A deliberately verbose subsection heading that tests hierarchy, line spacing, and the keep-with-next rule at the smallest supported page size {#sec-long-subheading}

This paragraph belongs to the preceding heading. The pagination engines should
move both elements when there is not enough room for the heading and at least a
useful beginning of its text. Web and EPUB layouts cannot promise a physical
page boundary, but their print and reader pagination styles should express the
same preference.

#### A long local detail heading remains unnumbered even when it wraps across more than one display line {#sec-long-detail-heading}

The local heading completes the hierarchy stress case. It must not acquire a
four-part number or appear in the contents simply because its text happens to
wrap. Narrow screens should reflow it without horizontal scrolling, while both
PDF backends should retain the same semantic level and broadly similar visual
weight.

## Boundary paragraphs for widow and orphan prevention {#sec-boundary-paragraphs}

The following paragraphs are intentionally similar in length but not identical.
Their labels let a reviewer locate the beginning and end of a paragraph in
extracted PDF text. At least one paragraph should cross a page boundary in each
PDF profile, and neither side of that boundary should contain only one line.

**Boundary Alpha begins.** A technical book rarely presents an uninterrupted
wall of prose, yet ordinary paragraphs still need dependable pagination. A
small edit early in a chapter can move every later line, so hand-tuned page
breaks are brittle and should not be part of the manuscript. The template must
instead ask the typesetter to keep a lone first or last line with its paragraph.
That policy may leave a little additional space at the bottom of a page, which
is preferable to separating a line from the thought it supports. Reviewers
should compare the smallest trim first because its narrower measure and shorter
page make boundary failures easiest to expose. The same source then tests the
larger print and review profiles without conditional prose. **Boundary Alpha
ends.**

**Boundary Bravo begins.** Stable pagination is a property of the complete
system rather than a single template instruction. Font metrics determine line
breaks; line spacing determines how many baselines fit; headings and figures
consume variable space; and the active language changes hyphenation. For that
reason the locked fonts and typesetter versions are part of this test. If a
dependency upgrade changes a paragraph from twelve lines to eleven, the exact
page may change while the acceptance rule remains constant: a split paragraph
needs at least two lines on both pages. This is also why the fixture uses normal
sentences instead of forced line breaks. It exercises the pagination algorithm
that real chapters will use and makes any failure representative rather than
ceremonial. **Boundary Bravo ends.**

**Boundary Charlie begins.** A good book page balances several competing
values. Even color along the bottom edge is attractive, but mechanical
uniformity is not worth a conspicuous widow, an orphaned heading, or distorted
word spacing. The PDF profiles therefore treat widow and orphan prevention as
a strong rule while allowing the page builder to resolve the remaining space.
The browser and EPUB styles declare the same minimum where paged-media support
exists, although an e-reader ultimately controls its own viewport, font size,
and pagination engine. The template documents that distinction instead of
claiming identical line and page breaks across fixed and reflowable outputs.
What remains universal is the source structure and the intended reading order.
**Boundary Charlie ends.**

**Boundary Delta begins.** Headings require a related but distinct rule. A
heading stranded at the foot of a page is not technically a paragraph widow,
yet it creates the same interruption for a reader. Each backend should keep a
heading with the block that follows it, including when the heading itself wraps
to two or three lines. The rule applies to sections, subsections, and local
detail headings; chapter openers already begin on a fresh recto page. Lists,
figures, code, and display equations can complicate keep-with-next behavior, so
later technical-authoring phases will add focused fixtures for those elements.
This phase establishes the prose baseline and ensures that an ordinary heading
followed by an ordinary paragraph behaves consistently. **Boundary Delta
ends.**

**Boundary Echo begins.** Intentional blank pages have a different purpose from
the small areas of flexible space produced by paragraph pagination. In a
two-sided book, a blank verso can preserve a right-hand opening for a major
division. Such a page must be genuinely blank: no running title, folio, rule,
or accidental placeholder should remain. The front matter includes a stable
blank verso for an automated check, while chapter and appendix transitions may
add other blanks as the preceding content expands or contracts. Reflowable
formats omit these sheets because recto and verso do not exist in a continuous
web page and are reader-controlled in an EPUB. This medium-specific behavior is
intentional rather than a loss of manuscript content. **Boundary Echo ends.**

**Boundary Foxtrot begins.** Physical page parity is counted from the first PDF
page, where page one is a recto. Printed folios may use roman numerals, arabic
numbers, or no visible number at all, so they are not reliable inputs to an
automated parity test. The validator instead searches each physical page for a
unique opening sentence and checks that the matching page number is odd. It
also confirms that the fixed front-matter verso contains no extractable text.
These assertions are deliberately independent of exact total page counts. The
specimen can grow throughout the roadmap without requiring a list of hard-coded
chapter pages, and a newly inserted illustration can move an opener while the
recto guarantee continues to pass. **Boundary Foxtrot ends.**

## A second long section title verifies that running furniture adapts after a page boundary without replacing the canonical heading {#sec-running-head-stress}

Running furniture should help a reader orient within an open book without
competing with the manuscript. A full chapter or section title can be much
longer than the available header measure, especially at 6 x 9 inches. The page
body, contents, bookmarks, and links retain the complete title; the furniture
must stay inside its reserved area and may use a compact rendering.
The following boundary paragraphs provide enough flow for both odd and even
running heads to appear during visual review.

**Boundary Golf begins.** Mirrored pages reverse the relationship between the
binding and the outside edge. Inside margins reserve room for binding and
handling, while outside margins carry the easiest-to-find folio. A running head
must honor that geometry on both odd and even pages. It should not collide with
the page number, cross the rule beneath the header, or expand downward into the
first body line. Long titles reveal those errors quickly because they exhaust
the available horizontal space. The stress case is therefore intentionally
more verbose than a recommended production heading, but it remains valid prose
and valid document structure. A robust template handles it gracefully rather
than imposing an undocumented character limit on authors. **Boundary Golf
ends.**

**Boundary Hotel begins.** Recto chapter starts are a print-profile decision,
not an instruction an author should sprinkle through source files. Both PDF
backends receive the policy from their page systems and may insert an empty
verso when the preceding division ends on a recto. Because the insertion is
automatic, the same chapter file works in the web book, EPUB, and any future
single-sided review format. The test searches for this chapter's unique opening
sentence and for openings in the ordinary reference chapter and appendices. It
will fail if a backend upgrade changes one of those divisions to an even
physical page. This gives the project a structural safeguard without freezing
the layout to one exact manuscript length. **Boundary Hotel ends.**

**Boundary India begins.** A long heading also tests navigation surfaces that
are easy to overlook during a PDF-only review. The web sidebar must wrap or
truncate without widening the viewport, the EPUB navigation document must
retain meaningful text, and the PDF contents entry must lead to the correct
destination. Decorative running furniture cannot become the only place where
a shortened form appears. Readers using assistive technology or search depend
on the semantic heading, while readers scanning a printed spread benefit from
the compact header. Keeping those roles separate permits an eventual explicit
short-title feature without compromising the canonical chapter name used by
links and metadata. **Boundary India ends.**

**Boundary Juliett begins.** Page composition must remain reproducible enough
to diagnose change without pretending that every renderer produces identical
typography. LuaLaTeX and Typst use different shaping, line-breaking, and page-
building algorithms. Small differences are expected, but clipped text, single
line widows or orphans, furniture on intentional blanks, and left-hand chapter
openers are defects in either backend. The acceptance checks therefore focus on
invariants rather than pixel equality. A reviewer can still compare rendered
pages for rhythm and hierarchy, and the build report records artifacts useful
for investigating a change. This combination of automated invariants and
targeted visual review scales better than treating one backend as a screenshot
of the other. **Boundary Juliett ends.**

**Boundary Kilo begins.** Reflowable media place a different boundary around
the problem. A phone can wrap this paragraph into many short lines, an EPUB
reader can replace the selected face or enlarge it, and a browser print dialog
can choose an arbitrary sheet. CSS can communicate preferred widow, orphan,
and heading-break behavior, but the reading system has final authority. The
template should degrade without hidden content or horizontal overflow when a
preference is unsupported. That means the source cannot depend on a blank page
for meaning, cannot reference facing-page position in essential instructions,
and cannot encode a heading as an image merely to preserve its line breaks.
Semantic prose remains the durable fallback across all of those environments.
**Boundary Kilo ends.**

**Boundary Lima begins.** The stress corpus is deliberately versioned beside
the template. When typography changes, these paragraphs move in realistic ways
and expose knock-on effects in page count, parity, furniture, and contents
layout. They are not meant to prescribe a writing style for the eventual books.
Once a real manuscript becomes a stronger test, the compact fixture can remain
as a quick regression case while selected production pages become visual
benchmarks. Until then, labeled starts and ends make it possible to discuss a
specific paragraph unambiguously across six PDF profiles and two independent
typesetters. The final criterion is simple: no reader should notice the page
builder while following the argument from one page to the next. **Boundary Lima
ends.**

## Review result {#sec-layout-review-result}

This chapter supplies the long-title, long-heading, pagination, and running-head
cases required by the Phase 2 review. Automated checks verify the stable blank
verso, division parity, complete marker text, and the presence of a paragraph
that crosses a page in each PDF. Visual review remains responsible for judging
line counts at those crossings and the quality of wrapping and white space.
